headline.phenotype_label: Genetically cardiometabolic, behaviourally under-recovered · APOE ε4 carrier · Early insulin resistance
headline.voice: Peer, systems-framed. Client #6 runs on dashboards — give him the causal chain and the smallest set of changes that move the most. The cardiovascular story is both his stated fear and his biggest genetic + biochemical risk, so it leads. The genome is fixed; its expression is not. Two items go to a physician first.

goal_alignment.his_words: I want my energy and focus back, and I don't want my dad's heart disease.
goal_alignment.how_protocol_serves_it: His 'energy and focus' is the under-recovery root (RC-2): fix sleep, caffeine timing and Zone-2 and the afternoon crash lifts. 'My dad's heart disease' is the genetic load (RC-1): the genome (ApoE ε4, Lp(a), 9p21) plus the blood (ApoB 105) say drive ApoB down hard — and the same Zone-2 + fat-quality work does both. One protocol, his two goals.

biological_age_trajectory.method: PhenoAge moves modestly because its inputs (glucose, hsCRP, RDW, WBC) only partly capture his risk — the big wins (ApoB, HOMA-IR, HDL, HRV, VO2max, NAFLD) live OUTSIDE the nine PhenoAge markers, which is exactly why the Deep panel + genome + wearable matter. Day-90 target reflects realistic hsCRP + glucose gains as inflammation and insulin sensitivity improve.

root_attack_pillars.name: Pillar 1 — Drive ApoB under 70 (offset the loaded genome)
anchor_interventions: Zone-2 cardio 150 min/week — the HDL + ApoB + insulin lever, and his 'energy' goal
Soluble fiber 10g/day (psyllium, oats, legumes) — veg-light, travel-proof
Saturated→unsaturated fat swap: cut ghee + fried orders, olive/mustard oil, halve dessert
Physician: aggressive-lipid + (SLCO1B1-informed) statin discussion; Lp(a) family screening

root_attack_pillars.name: Pillar 2 — Recover as hard as he works
anchor_interventions: Sleep 6→7.5h: fixed wake, phone out of the bedroom, 30-min wind-down
Caffeine cutoff 10:00 (CYP1A2 slow) — protects deep sleep + next-day HRV
One true recovery day/week; 10-min daily breathwork (COMT-matched)

root_attack_pillars.name: Pillar 3 — Reverse the early insulin resistance
anchor_interventions: Zone-2 + 2× resistance/week (muscle = glucose sink); raise VO2max off 38
Protein-forward, lower-glycemic, soluble-fiber meals that survive travel
Cut late dessert + weekly alcohol; earlier dinners
Visceral-fat loss — the common denominator across ApoB, TG, NAFLD, HDL, T

genomic_filter.finding: One ε4 copy — higher lifetime cardiovascular and Alzheimer's risk, and LDL/ApoB that respond more strongly to saturated fat.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Your ApoB target is set to <70 (not the usual <80–100), the fat profile goes Mediterranean, and Zone-2 + deep sleep are prioritized as brain-health levers, not just heart. We also offer a genetic-counseling conversation — this is a probability shift you can act on, not a verdict.

genomic_filter.finding: Genetically elevated Lp(a), confirmed in your blood — a lifelong, lifestyle-fixed cardiovascular amplifier.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Because Lp(a) itself won't move, we crush every other ApoB-mediated risk instead, and flag first-degree family Lp(a) screening (it's heritable). Common and under-tested in South Asians.

genomic_filter.finding: Two copies at the most-replicated coronary-artery-disease locus, acting independent of lipids.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Adds weight to early, aggressive ApoB control and an earlier clinician conversation — stacked with ApoE and Lp(a), the cardiovascular lever leads the whole plan.

genomic_filter.finding: One copy of the strongest common type-2-diabetes variant — lower insulin-secretion reserve.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Your early insulin resistance (HOMA-IR 2.9) matters more for you than for the average 40-year-old, so the metabolic lever is raised and we retest glucose/insulin earlier.

genomic_filter.finding: You clear caffeine slowly — afternoon coffee measurably hurts that night's sleep and next-day HRV.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Caffeine cutoff is 10:00 and ≤2 cups. Your own Whoop proves it: HRV crashes on the nights you have a late espresso (see Autopilot).

genomic_filter.finding: Intermediate statin-transporter function — modestly higher statin-myopathy risk.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: If your physician starts a statin for the lipid picture, this note favors a non-simvastatin choice or a lower dose. We don't prescribe — we hand the prescriber the data.

genomic_filter.finding: About 65% enzyme activity; with your homocysteine at 12.5, the active B-vitamin forms are preferred.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Your B-vitamin is methylfolate + methyl-B12, not folic acid — a small, targeted switch, not a stack.

genomic_filter.finding: Dopamine-clearance and BDNF traits that favor steady aerobic down-regulation.
genomic_filter.how_it_changed_the_protocol: Your stress lever leans on breathwork + Zone-2 (which you need anyway) rather than high-stimulant strategies — and aerobic exercise + sleep are doubly worthwhile for you.

autopilot_feed.patch: Skip the morning espresso (it'll deepen the debt). 20-min Zone-2 walk in daylight to lift HRV. Hold today's heavy session to tomorrow; keep it to mobility + a walk.

recovery_sleep.rationale: Sleep is the single highest-leverage lever he isn't pulling. ~6h with 11% deep sleep sits under his low HRV, his cortisol, his testosterone, his insulin resistance and his focus. Moving lights-out from ~00:45 to 23:00 buys ~1.5h at almost zero willpower cost.
recovery_sleep.wind_down_protocol: Phone charges outside the bedroom (he reads in bed now). 30-min wind-down: no laptop after 22:15, dim lights, magnesium glycinate at 22:30. Bedroom cool + dark.
recovery_sleep.caffeine_rule: Cutoff 10:00, ≤2 cups (CYP1A2 slow). Replace the 3pm coffee with a 10-min daylight walk — the Autopilot will reinforce this every time a late coffee tanks his HRV.
recovery_sleep.recovery_day: One true recovery day/week (Whoop-guided — when the 7-day HRV trend dips, that's the day).
recovery_sleep.travel_protocol: On red-eye nights: hydration + caffeine-before-10:00-local + 15-min daylight on landing; no training the next day.

leading_principles: Sustainable + portable beats severe — he eats out 6x/week and travels constantly.
Two structural moves: shift fat quality (less saturated) and add soluble fiber + protein; both lower ApoB AND improve insulin sensitivity.
ApoE ε4 makes the saturated-fat swap genuinely worth it for him specifically.
structural_changes: Swap ghee + restaurant fried items for olive/mustard oil; halve the after-dinner dessert
Add 1 tbsp psyllium daily + oats/chia at breakfast — the veg-light, travel-proof ApoB fiber move
Protein-forward every meal (eggs, dahi, chicken, fish, paneer, dal) to blunt glucose + satiety (FTO)
Order smarter: grilled over fried, double the dal/sabzi, brown/less rice, skip the naan-and-dessert combo
Earlier dinners when not traveling; cut the weekly investor-dinner drinks to ≤2
nutrition.fat_quality_note: Mediterranean-leaning per ApoE ε4: olive oil, nuts, fatty fish; minimise saturated fat.

leading_principles: His biggest gap is steady aerobic work (<30 min/week). Zone-2 is the top lever for HDL, ApoB, insulin sensitivity AND his 'energy' goal — and protects the ε4 brain.
He's exercise-poor, not over-trained (ACWR 0.58) — the job is to ADD a base, not redistribute.
Built around travel: most sessions need only shoes or a hotel gym.

weekly_structure.zone_2_detail: 3-4× 35-45 min at conversational pace (HR ~120-135) — incline treadmill, cycle, brisk walk, or hotel-gym cardio. Whoop confirms the zone.
weekly_structure.resistance_detail: 2× full-body (squat, hinge, push, pull, carry) — muscle is his glucose sink; portable dumbbell/bodyweight versions for travel.
weekly_structure.vo2max_sessions: 1 (optional, once the base is in — short intervals)

twelve_week_plan.detail: 2× Zone-2 (30 min) + 2× full-body strength + hit 8k steps. No intensity — just consistency and the caffeine/sleep rules.
3× Zone-2 (40 min) + 2× strength. Notice resting HR + how 'energy' starts to return. Book the physician (lipid) visit.
3-4× Zone-2 + add 1 short interval session once recovery is solid. Week 8 lighter (travel-heavy). Resistance progresses.
Hold the structure. No heavy training 48h before the Day-90 retest.

mind_wellness.daily_practice: 10-min breathwork (physiological sigh or box breathing) — he does none, and his stress sits 8/10 in a fundraise. COMT Val/Met favors this steady down-regulation over more stimulants.

mind_wellness.stress_note: The fundraise stress is real and situational. The levers are sleep + breathwork + Zone-2, not a supplement. Caffeine moderation is itself an anxiety lever for a slow metabolizer.

outcome_expectations.expectation: Afternoon crash eases within 3-4 weeks of fixed sleep + caffeine timing + Zone-2; HRV trend up on the Whoop
ApoB 105→<85 by Day 90 on lifestyle alone, toward <70 with the physician-decided statin; HDL up, TG down
HOMA-IR 2.9→<2.0; glucose under 95; NAFLD enzymes (ALT/GGT) trending down with visceral-fat loss
Neither changes — they're genetic. The win is everything they amplify, driven down hard, and a clear plan instead of his father's surprise.

what_not_to_change: Don't jump to TRT for the testosterone 420 — it's downstream of sleep, stress and visceral fat; fix the roots and it follows.
Don't over-restrict food — he travels and eats out; portability + protein + fiber beats a rigid diet he'll abandon.
Don't add a supplement stack — six targeted items, not twenty.
